name: a-aerial-wall-between
idea: Beat A. A straight-down aerial photograph in the manner of large-format landscape documentary: the frame is split by a single long wall running across it. In the top half, a gated estate of identical white villas with turquoise private pools, perfect lawns, utterly empty and still. In the bottom half, pressed right up against the wall, a dense patchwork of tarpaulin shelters, cookfire smoke and laundry lines, tiny figures too small to read. Flat, even overcast light, deep focus, muted earth tones against the one shock of pool blue; it should look almost like an abstract painting until you understand it.

name: a-flash-banquet-left-standing
idea: Beat A. Night interior of a grand private dining room on a superyacht or penthouse, photographed with a harsh direct on-camera flash in saturated colour: a long table still laid for a feast that ended long ago, champagne flutes furred with dust, a melted ice sculpture now a puddle on silver, gold chairs pushed back as if everyone left in a hurry. Through the floor-to-ceiling windows behind, pitch darkness with a few distant fires on a shoreline. Eye-level mid shot looking down the length of the table, hard flash shadows on the wall, no people. Comic, garish and sad at once.

name: a-painted-bored-suburb
idea: Beat A. A painterly, digitally painted illustration in a calm, melancholy Scandinavian-suburb mood: a quiet two-lane road at late-afternoon golden hour, a child of about ten on a bicycle in the foreground looking away from the camera, bored. On the horizon, dwarfing the low houses, enormous derelict windowless server halls and cooling towers, dark and silent, with wild grass growing to their fences and a hand-painted barrier across the road. Wide shot from child's eye height, soft hazy light, long shadows, cold-blue distance against warm foreground. It should feel like arriving long after the disaster, when everyone has stopped talking about it.

name: a-kerbside-furniture-deadpan
idea: Beat A. A deadpan, straight-on large-format colour photograph of an ordinary street of identical small terraced houses at flat noon light under a pale sky. Outside every single front door, the whole contents of each home sit stacked on the pavement: sofas, cots, a fridge, framed photos face-down, boxes in the rain, all left out like an eviction day that happened to the entire street at once. Front doors are boarded with fresh plywood. Shot from the middle of the empty road with deep focus and a symmetrical vanishing point; nobody visible; the banality is the horror.

name: b-grey-tableau-office
idea: Beat B. A static, centred tableau with shadowless flat light and a pale grey-green, desaturated palette, like an absurdist Swedish film set: BadCode sits behind a small, bare municipal desk in an otherwise empty waiting-room office, full figure visible, gloved hands folded neatly on the desk, staring straight down the lens. The balaclava is plain dark knit with a thin white ring around the wearer's left eye hole and a small rounded red triangle inside the ring at about 2 o'clock, pointing down. A wilted rubber plant, a wall clock with no hands, one empty visitor chair. Deep focus, wide-ish 35mm, camera at seated eye height; polite, patient, faintly tragic.

name: b-fireside-public-information
idea: Beat B. A warm, grainy 16mm look of a 1970s public-information broadcast: BadCode sits in a wingback armchair in a cosy living room with patterned brown-and-orange wallpaper, a standard lamp glowing tungsten beside it, a cup of tea on a doily. Medium close-up from chest up, slightly soft focus, gentle vignette, faded film colours. Plain dark knitted balaclava, thin white ring around the wearer's left eye hole with a small rounded red triangle at about 2 o'clock pointing down, black leather gloves resting on the armrests. Looking directly into the lens with the calm of someone about to explain the household budget.

name: b-flash-doorstep-closeup
idea: Beat B. A tight close-up at night, lit only by a harsh direct camera flash, saturated and slightly overexposed in the centre: the masked face fills most of the vertical frame, dark knitted balaclava with every fibre visible, a thin white ring around the wearer's left eye hole and a small rounded red triangle inside it at about 2 o'clock, pointing down, the white and red catching the flash. Background falls to near black, with only the edge of a front-door frame and a doorbell light visible. Eyes level with the lens, unblinking, the stillness of a polite caller who knows exactly what happens next. One gloved hand raised in a small, courteous wave at the edge of frame.

name: b-standing-in-the-drained-pool
idea: Beat B, tying the future to the figure: BadCode stands alone, upright and perfectly centred, at the deep end of a drained, cracked luxury swimming pool with brown leaves and a broken sun lounger at its bottom; the empty villa looms pale above the pool edge. Shot from slightly low at the shallow end with a 28mm lens, symmetrical, deep focus, under a flat white overcast sky. Plain dark knitted balaclava with a thin white ring around the wearer's left eye hole and a small rounded red triangle inside at about 2 o'clock pointing down; gloved hands clasped behind the back like a tour guide. Muted, chalky palette; the stillness is the joke.

name: c-blue-hour-empty-horizon
idea: Beat C, the clean button frame for the logo: a very calm, minimalist seascape at blue hour, a perfectly flat still sea taking the bottom fifth of the vertical frame with a thin line of a distant low coast, and above it a huge smooth gradient of sky from deep indigo at the top to a faint warm glow at the horizon. One tiny warm light on the far coast, nothing else. Long exposure smoothness, no clouds, no birds, generous empty space in the upper and middle frame where a logo will sit. Quiet, hopeful after everything before it.
